title: Health map
purpose: Turn a person's medical history into a map that answers three questions on any date: what is going on, how bad is it, and what happens next. Every number carries its source; anything generated is marked as unconfirmed.

tool_notes.pubmed: the only free source of the numbers behind a prognosis: hazard ratios with a confidence interval, so a prediction cites something instead of guessing
tool_notes.a web-search tool: guidelines (ESC, USPSTF) live in PDFs on society sites, not in an index — a search finds the document, nothing else will

kinds.meaning: a diagnosis, confirmed or suspected. Carries onset and status, never a date of its own
a measured value or a whole panel. Value is a number, unit is separate, reference range comes from the lab
kinds.keywords: lab, test, result, value, panel, LOINC

kinds.meaning: a visit, an appointment, a hospital stay — anything a person attended
a drug and a regimen, with a start and, when it ended, a stop
something done to the person: surgery, an endoscopy, a dressing. Carries the date it was performed and the document it was recorded in
kinds.keywords: procedure, surgery, operation, endoscopy, intervention, SNOMED, ICD-10-PCS

kinds.meaning: a period rolled up: annual (stamped 01-01) or today. Virtual, generated, never an event somebody recorded
a simulated projection under a condition. It does not move the main estimate until the condition is met
the document a fact came from: a discharge note, a scan, a printout. Carries the date printed on it and is the provenance, so it points at no source of its own

kind_notes.one word per thing: `observation` covers a single marker and a whole panel — a panel is several observations with `part_of` edges, not a new kind. A kind is what a node IS; the everyday words are keywords.
kind_notes.six of the eight are events: an event is a fact in the record with a date in `when` and, unless it is the document itself, a `source` naming the document it came from: condition, observation, encounter, medication, procedure, document. A summary is a virtual marker and a prediction is a simulation — visible, dated where they need to be, and never events.
kind_notes.no free-form kinds: the template has a layout for each of the eight kinds and nothing for the rest. A kind that is not on this list is a modelling error, and `validate` refuses it.

edges.label: treated by
edges.meaning: that condition is treated with this drug
edges.name: treated_by

edges.label: contradicts
edges.meaning: a later measurement disagrees with the earlier note — draw it, do not hide it
edges.name: contradicts

edges.label: derived from
edges.meaning: provenance: this fact came from that document. Required for every fact that came from a document
edges.name: derived_from

edges.label: advised
edges.meaning: a doctor recommended it — distinct from the patient actually starting it
edges.name: advised

edges.label: projected
edges.meaning: what the prediction is about. A prediction under an unmet condition is drawn hollow and never moves the estimate
edges.name: projected

edge_notes.closed list: a new relation needs an entry in docs/DATA-CONTRACT.md first, then in this file, then in the engine. Not the other way round.
edge_notes.label is human, name is machine: `label` is what a person reads in the catalogue; `name` is the token that goes into an edge's `label` in a document and must be one of the contract's relations (`tracks`, `treated_by`, `derived_from`, `part_of`, …). The skill seeds a graph from `name`, so a space in it makes every graph this app creates non-conformant — `scripts/app-manifest.test.ts` guards exactly that.
edge_notes.temporal edges: an edge carries valid_from and valid_to when the relation itself is temporary. A relation that was true and is not true now is closed, not deleted.

visuals.node weight: `weight` on a node is what it is worth on this map, and how it was measured is stated once for the whole graph in `meta.weight.metric`. Every panel says which of the two a node's number came from: the document, or the graph's own connections.
visuals.node style: `solid` = confirmed fact, `hollow` = generated or unconfirmed, `skull` = contradicted or dangerous. The style is the honesty flag, not decoration.
visuals.direction: `dir: in` puts an arrowhead at the `to` end, so a measurement points at the condition it watches and a prediction points at what it projects.
visuals.level: a node's position on the third axis. Documents at the bottom, then what was measured and attended, then what it means, then what we expect. The 3D view is the only place it moves anything.

notes.what they are: the long form of a node's description, one markdown file per node in a `docs/` folder beside the graph document: what a test measures, what a diagnosis means in plain words, where the claim comes from.
notes.why they are required: a condition or an observation node carries a plain-language sentence from the moment it is created — a number without a meaning is exactly the thing this app exists to fix.
notes.how they are read: they are inlined into the rendered page (a page opened from `file://` cannot fetch its neighbours) and opened from a node's 'read the note' button.
notes.the two export skills: `markers-to-pdf` and `markers-to-fhir` walk the markers of the main view out of a kg.json — one paginated PDF for a reader, one HL7 FHIR R4 bundle for another system — and write nothing back. They live at `skills/` in this repo, are fetched by `kg check --install` from `skills_url`, and are never a screen: a template app has no write path, and an export is what it has instead.
notes.the skill that writes: `add-prediction` is the one skill here that writes to the document: one PubMed paper, its published ratio and interval, a check that the person belongs to the population that was studied, and then the paper's `document` node, the `prediction` and the `projected` edge. It refuses without a PMID and it leaves both nodes `confirmed: false` — a human reading the paper is what turns a forecast into a confirmed one, and a skill cannot pretend to be that human. `docs/ADD-PREDICTION.md` is the long form.

scale.the budget: a person's history is hundreds of events, not thousands of papers: 200–2000 nodes is the expected range, and a graph of that size draws without collapsing on a laptop.
scale.what happens past it: the viewer collapses the smallest, weakest clusters and says how many nodes it hid, with a button to expand anyway.

level_note: where a kind sits on the fold axis when a node of that kind carries no `level` of its own. Documents at the bottom, then what was measured and attended, then what it means, then what we expect. The document always wins.
notes_for_agents: This app is a document reader, not a medical device. It never diagnoses and never prescribes. Every number carries a source or it is not drawn; generated content carries `not confirmed` until a human confirms it. Data lives in kg.json and sources/ — never in the template.
status: template not shipped yet: app.json is final, the HTML build is tasks T11 and T26 in docs/PLAN-health-2026-11-12.md
